Opensidian 0.9.5-RC2 is the second release candidate of 0.9.5, a feature and bug-fix release on top of 0.9.4. It supersedes 0.9.5-RC1 (tag `v0.9.5`), which stays available for download. The app version is still 0.9.5, so the files are named `opensidian-0.9.5-*`. The downloads are the same as 0.9.4 (two AppImages, Flatpak, RPM, DEB), and now come for Linux aarch64 as well as x86_64.

Every file below has a GitHub artifact attestation (SLSA build provenance) proving it was built by this repository's `release.yml` workflow on GitHub-hosted runners.

**SHA256SUMS is GPG-signed by the maintainer** (`SHA256SUMS.asc`, key `A6E6 9ED6 BC47 79F3 2817  2148 4CC1 AFDE 15B6 4EA3`, the same key as 0.9.5-RC1 and v0.9.4).

**The RPMs are not signed.** No RPM signing key is used in CI. Check the RPMs like every other file: with `SHA256SUMS` and `gh attestation verify` (see Verification).

## New since 0.9.5-RC1

### Workspaces (#94)
- The Workspaces core plugin: save the current layout (splits, tabs, open files, sidebars) under a name, then load, rename or delete saved layouts. Use the **Manage workspace layouts** ribbon button or the commands **Workspaces: Manage workspace layouts**, **Save current layout** and **Load workspace layout**. Layouts are stored in Obsidian's `.obsidian/workspaces.json` format, so they work in both apps, and they stay with their vault. A layout is not loaded while a note has unsaved changes. The manager shows the saved layouts as soon as it opens. (PR #191)
- In a very short window, the left ribbon clips its last icons like Obsidian instead of drawing them outside the window. Closing a graph also frees its background worker; before, opening and closing graphs could leave one running per graph for as long as the window was open. (PR #192)

### Properties (#119)
- A Properties block at the top of a note in Live Preview, like Obsidian: text, list, number, checkbox, date and date & time properties, plus tags, aliases and cssclasses. Add, rename, delete and change the type of a property (types are saved in `.obsidian/types.json`); names and values suggest what the vault already uses. **Add file property** (Ctrl+;, also in the tab menu) adds a row and creates the frontmatter if the note has none. Reading view shows the block read-only. (PR #125)
- The setting **Properties in document** (Settings → Editor): Visible, Hidden or Source. (PR #125)
- The **Properties view** in the right sidebar (command **Properties view: Show all properties**) lists every property in the vault with its count, sorts by name or frequency, searches a property on click, changes its type and renames it across the vault. (PR #125)
- Editing a property rewrites only that property's lines; the rest of the frontmatter stays byte for byte the same. Frontmatter that is not valid YAML is shown as source and never rewritten, and entries the editor does not understand (comments, nested maps, block scalars) are shown read-only. (PR #125)

### Editor
- Pasting rich text (for example from a web page) inserts it as Markdown, keeping links and formatting, like Obsidian. An image on the clipboard still embeds, and plugins that handle paste still come first. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes plain text. Italic is written as `*text*` (Obsidian writes `_text_`). (#143, PR #146)
- Scroll positions are kept by the editor itself: switching between Live Preview and Source, reopening a tab, going back and forward, jumping to a heading or a search result, and changing the font size land on the line you were on, also below tall embeds such as images. (#125, #137, PR #148)

### Tabs and window
- Double-click a tab to rename its note or canvas inline in the tab. A single click only switches to the tab. The inline title of a note is also edited on double-click only, and shows a pointer cursor instead of a text cursor. F2 and the tab menu's **Rename...** work as before. (#142, PR #147)
- The empty space in the left and right sidebars' top tab headers drags the window, like the middle tab row. Clicking a sidebar tab icon still only switches the view. (#141, PR #150)

### Bookmarks and audio
- Dragging an image, PDF or audio recording tab onto Bookmarks bookmarks the file. (#140, PR #151)
- Clicking an audio recording in the explorer or in Bookmarks opens it in an audio view with a player. (#140, PR #151)

### Daily notes and Audio recorder on by default (#139)
- Daily notes and Audio recorder are now on by default, in new vaults and in vaults that have no setting for them. If you turned one off, it stays off. (PR #145)
- Both work in a restricted vault. There, an audio recording plays only after you press Play: nothing loads or decodes it before that. In a trusted vault, recordings load when they come into view, as before. (PR #145)

### Fixes to the changes above
- Found by testing after the changes above were merged, fixed before this release: a link to a heading in the same note scrolls the heading into view, and a note with a Properties block or with images that load late keeps its line when you switch between Live Preview and Source. (PR #182)

## Features in 0.9.5 (from RC1)

### Daily notes (#115)
- The Daily notes core plugin: open today's note (and the previous or next one) from the ribbon or the command palette, with Obsidian's settings for the date format, the folder, the template and opening on startup. Settings are stored in Obsidian's `daily-notes.json`. (PR #122)

### Audio recorder (#116)
- The Audio recorder core plugin records from the microphone into a `.webm` file in the attachment folder and inserts it at the cursor. Audio embeds such as `![[recording.webm]]` play inline in Live Preview and reading view. Only the recorder can use the microphone, never a community plugin. The AppImages use the distro's GStreamer plugins for recording (base and good). (PR #124)

### Downloads
- Linux aarch64 downloads: both AppImages, the Flatpak, the RPM and the DEB are now also built for aarch64, natively on GitHub's arm runners. (#97, PR #107)

## Fixes in 0.9.5 (from RC1)
- Explorer and Bookmarks: renaming a file or a bookmark edits the name inline in its row, like Obsidian. (#101, PR #105)
- Images open in an image view when you open them from the explorer or from Bookmarks. (#102, PR #104)
- A link dragged in from a browser lands as `[title](url)`. Before, the drop was lost. (#51, PR #109)
- Templater: **Insert template** keeps the template's properties. (#95, PR #108)
- A bookmarked graph saves your changes to its settings back to its bookmark. (#118, PR #120)
- Faster startup on big vaults: the vault index is built off the main thread while the window opens. On a 20,001-note test vault, the extra startup time over a 2-note vault went from 1214 ms to 379 ms (median of 3 cold opens). The explorer shows the complete vault as before. (#106, PR #121)
- Choosing the default theme by name now paints like having no theme set. (#96, PR #103)
- The graph's settings button shows the stock cog icon. (#130, PR #133)
- Security: if a trusted vault's directory is replaced by a different one at the same path, the new directory no longer inherits the old one's plugin trust. (#127, PR #129)

### Packaging and build
- The supply-chain and code scanners in CI run on develop, main and release branches only. (#123, #131)
- The Flatpak metadata lists the 0.9.5 release.

## Known issues
- Audio recorder: while the recorder is recording, a plugin that asks for the microphone at the same moment can still get a stream for an instant. The stream is ended right away and never stays live. (#136)
- Switching into Live Preview can land a fraction of a line (about 8 px) above the line you were on, so the line can sit at the very top edge. Obsidian keeps the pixel offset instead and can be off by many lines on the same note.
- The first click after scrolling with the keyboard can be ignored. This was already there before 0.9.5.
- The AppImages, deb and rpm need glibc 2.43 or newer (built on Ubuntu 26), so they do not start on older distros such as Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Debian 12. Opensidian supports current distros only. On an older distro, use the Flatpak, which brings its own runtime.

## Verification
Download every file of this release into one directory, then:

```sh
# 1. checksums: every file must report OK
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 2. build provenance: each file was built by this repository's
#    release workflow on GitHub Actions
for f in opensidian-0.9.5-x86_64* opensidian-0.9.5-aarch64* SHA256SUMS; do
  gh attestation verify "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done

# 3. release attestation: this release is immutable; the tag and
#    every file are pinned by a GitHub release attestation
gh release verify v0.9.5-rc2 -R jpzk/opensidian
for f in opensidian-0.9.5-x86_64* opensidian-0.9.5-aarch64* SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.asc; do
  gh release verify-asset v0.9.5-rc2 "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done
```

The RPMs are unsigned, so `rpm -K` reports no signature. Use the checks above for them.

**Signature:** `SHA256SUMS` is signed by the maintainer. Import the key from https://github.com/jpzk.gpg and check it with `gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS`. The key fingerprint is `A6E6 9ED6 BC47 79F3 2817  2148 4CC1 AFDE 15B6 4EA3`.
